title: GPU tenancy fairness: boundary guards, throttling predicates, and quota escalation flow
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a set of programmable "boundary guards" for dedicated GPU pools that deliver tenant separation guarantees, predictable per-tenant throughput, and practical noisy-neighbor mitigation without unacceptable utilization loss.

Scope: design and implement admission control + enforcement primitives that work at the request-routing and pod/container scheduling layer for Dedicated clusters. This ticket covers: (1) soft vs hard quota semantics, (2) throttling predicates and token-bucket burst windows, (3) eviction ramps and grace windows for long-running KV cache heavy workloads, (4) a quota escalation/appeal flow for tenants to request short-term bursts, and (5) the observability and alerting rules to detect contention and debug noisy neighbors.

Non-goals: full multi-tenant scheduler rewrite; replacing cloud provider quota enforcement; cross-cluster global throttling (handled in a follow-up).

Design highlights:
- Admission control at the routing layer: requests carry a tenancy token and cost vector (estimated concurrency and nominal tokens). Router consults a local quota agent which enforces per-tenant concurrency limits and token-bucket rates before allocating to GPU pooled workers.
- Soft quota: allows short bursts up to a configured burst_window (e.g., 30s) with exponentially decaying grace. Soft-burst consumption is metered and emits signals for billing/alerts.
- Hard quota: strict concurrency/VRAM caps enforced by preemption policy. When exceeded, new requests return 429 with structured retry-after and suggested model-variant fallback.
- Eviction ramp: long-lived KV-heavy sessions are placed on an eviction ladder where the system progressively reduces allowed inflight tokens, issues warnings, and finally preempts cached KV slots while preserving partial progress via checkpointing.
- Throttling predicates: a small DSL of predicates (utilization > X, p95 latency > Y, free_memory < Z, tenant_error_rate spike) used by autoscaler and admission control to decide throttle vs scale vs preempt.
- Fairness algorithm: experiment with weighted Dominant Resource Fairness (wDRF) per-tenant using GPU-memory and GPU-concurrency as dominant resources.
- Escalation flow: tenants can request temporary burst via API (timeboxed) which creates a short-lived reservation slice granted only if headroom and SLO budgets permit. All approvals are auditable and emit audit events for billing/chargeback.
acceptance_criteria: Router-level quota agent enforces per-tenant token-bucket rates with configurable burst_window and persistent meters
Soft bursts allow short-lived SLO-friendly spikes without immediate preemption and generate observability events
Hard quota triggers predictable 429 with retry semantics and optional model-variant fallback configured per-tenant
Eviction ramp preemption preserves checkpoint data and reduces KV-resident footprint gracefully within configured grace window
Throttling predicate DSL implemented and integrated with autoscaler decision path
Dashboard shows per-tenant utilization, burst consumption, preemptions, and p99 latency with alerting thresholds
Canary rollout on 3 Dedicated clusters, no customer-visible SLO degradation during canary
comments: 2026-01-18 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded. Agreed to separate admission control (routing) from scheduler changes; will prototype admission agent as sidecar first.

2026-01-25 - Diego Ramos: Initial prototype of token-bucket agent committed to feature branch. It enforces concurrency and burst tokens at the router. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/482
2026-02-02 - PM review (Samir Patel): Please ensure billing and audit events for soft-burst consumption. Also flag security review for escalation API. Added 'security_review_required'.
2026-02-11 - Design feedback (Maya Ortiz): Suggest using model-variant fallback instead of outright 429 for 'best-effort' pricing tiers. Added fallback hooks to router response metadata.

2026-02-20 - Perf run: Synthetic noisy-neighbor test (10 tenants, one generates KV-heavy long sessions) shows p95 latency increase of 15% before soft quotas applied. After enabling soft-burst, p95 stabilized; however overall GPU utilization dropped 4%. Next step: tune burst_window and wDRF weights.
2026-02-28 - Security (Nadia Kim): Reviewed escalation API auth flow. Recommend short-lived signed requests and KMS-backed approval tokens. Minor comments added to Confluence doc.

2026-03-03 - Diego Ramos: Completed integration tests for eviction ramp and checkpointing. Using synthetic checkpoint store to validate no data loss on preemption. Preparing canary config for three clusters (canary tags: gcc-canary-1..3).
2026-03-04 - PM (Samir Patel): Added customer impact notes and requested due_date 2026-04-15 to align with dedicated-2026.04 release
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable routing-side token-bucket enforcement and soft-burst metering on 3 Dedicated clusters (1 week). Monitor p99/p95 latency, preemptions, and utilization. Phase 2 (pilot): enable eviction-ramp for 10 pilot tenants and gate hard-quota preemption behind operator flag (2 weeks). Phase 3 (gradual): enable hard quotas + escalation API for all Dedicated customers with advisory notices (4 weeks). Rollback: disable token-bucket at router and revert canary tag; preemptions are reversible because eviction ramp checkpointing preserves client state.
